avoid.reason: Beautiful by day on the Caminito strip, but muggings just a block away — don’t wander, especially at night.
The Villa 31 shantytown by Retiro station and Constitución/Once are pickpocket-prone.

hood_desc: Palermo is the citys largest and trendiest barrio, split into subzones like Palermo Soho and Hollywood, packed with boutiques, street art, leafy parks and a nonstop cafe and nightlife scene. It suits younger travelers, digital nomads and anyone wanting hip restaurants and bars within walking distance.

Recoleta is elegant and refined, known for grand French-style architecture, upscale hotels, museums and the famous cemetery where Eva Peron is buried. It suits travelers who want a quieter, sophisticated and safe neighborhood with a European feel.

San Telmo is the historic bohemian heart of the city, full of cobblestone streets, antique shops, tango halls and a lively Sunday market. It suits culture lovers and budget-minded travelers who embrace a gritty, artistic and authentic old-world atmosphere.

La Boca is a colorful working-class barrio famous for the painted houses of Caminito, tango dancers and the Boca Juniors stadium. It is vibrant and photogenic by day but rougher around the edges, best for a guided daytime visit rather than staying overnight.

Puerto Madero is the modern, polished waterfront district built around restored docks, with glass skyscrapers, luxury hotels, upscale restaurants and a nature reserve nearby. It suits business travelers and those seeking safety, space and sleek contemporary comfort over historic charm.

water.note: Tap water is treated and officially safe to drink; some travelers ease in with bottled water first.

transit.pay: Load a rechargeable SUBE card (sold/topped up at kiosks, post offices and stations; foreigners need their passport, or use the airport tourist kiosk) or tap a contactless bank card/phone at the turnstiles. A single subte ride costs roughly ARS 1,600-2,500 depending on card registration (about $1.20-2).
transit.hours: The Subte runs about 5am-11pm on weekdays with shorter weekend hours; there is no night service.

landmarks: Obelisco de Buenos Aires
The 67-meter obelisk on Avenida 9 de Julio is the city's most recognizable monument and central photo icon.
Casa Rosada
The pink presidential palace on Plaza de Mayo is instantly recognizable and steeped in Argentine political history.
Teatro Colón
One of the world's finest opera houses, celebrated for its opulent Beaux-Arts facade and gilded interior.
La Recoleta Cemetery
An extraordinary necropolis of elaborate mausoleums, including Eva Perón's tomb, prized for dramatic architectural photography.
Caminito (La Boca)
A vibrant open-air museum street lined with brightly painted corrugated houses, tango dancers, and colorful facades.
Puente de la Mujer
A sleek, sail-shaped pedestrian bridge by Santiago Calatrava that anchors the modern Puerto Madero waterfront.
Floralis Genérica
A giant kinetic steel flower sculpture in Plaza de las Naciones Unidas that opens and closes with the sun.
Palacio del Congreso
The grand domed seat of Argentina's National Congress, a Beaux-Arts landmark facing the historic Plaza del Congreso.
Catedral Metropolitana
Buenos Aires' neoclassical cathedral, notable as the former parish of Pope Francis and its striking columned facade.
Plaza de Mayo
The historic central square surrounded by Casa Rosada and the Cathedral, the political and symbolic heart of the city.

train.note: There are no international passenger trains from Buenos Aires. Long-distance domestic trains leave from Retiro and Constitución for Rosario, Córdoba, Tucumán and Mar del Plata; seats are cheap and sell out weeks ahead, so book early on the SOFSE site.

bus.note: International coaches leave from the Retiro bus terminal (Terminal de Ómnibus Retiro). Bring your passport. For Montevideo the cross-river ferry is usually quicker than the long overland bus, so check the ferry section first.

ferry.note: Fast ferries cross the Río de la Plata from the Puerto Madero terminals to Colonia and Montevideo — passport required. Buquebus also sells combined ferry-plus-bus tickets onward to Montevideo and Punta del Este. Colonia Express sails from Dársena Norte.

half.name: San Isidro

half.name: La Plata

half.name: Luján
